approach: Write the time each car takes to reach the same finish distance from rest, then form the given time difference and speed difference and divide one by the other.

steps.text: Let d be the distance to the finish line. Since both cars start from rest with constant acceleration, write each car's time to cover d.
steps.equation: d = ½a₁t_A² ⟹ t_A = √(2d/a₁), d = ½a₂t_B² ⟹ t_B = √(2d/a₂)

steps.text: Car A takes a time t less than car B, so form t_B minus t_A.
Car A's finishing speed exceeds car B's by v, so form v_A minus v_B using v = at for each car.
Divide the speed difference by the time difference; the common factor √(2d)(√a₁ − √a₂) cancels.
steps.why_this_step: Both v and t were written in terms of the same distance d, so d cancels out of the ratio and only a₁, a₂, t remain.

final_answer.value: v = √(a₁a₂) t, proved by expressing t = t_B − t_A and v = v_A − v_B in terms of the common finishing distance d and dividing.

common_mistakes.text: Using v = a₁t or v = a₂t with one shared t, instead of each car's own finish time, ignores the actual difference and gives no relation to the t and v of the problem.
